claims.text: Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started on 2026-08-01.
Patient is 84 years old and weighs 58 kg, per clinician note dated 2026-08-01.

The apixaban dose of 5 mg twice daily does not meet the label-specified reduction criteria: two of age ≥80, weight ≤60 kg, and creatinine ≥133 umol/L are present (age 84, weight 58 kg, creatinine 140 umol/L).

open_questions: What was the creatinine level before today's result of 140 umol/L, and when was it last measured?
Was renal function assessed prior to initiating apixaban, and what was the estimated CrCl or eGFR at that time?
Has apixaban been held, reduced, or discontinued in response to elevated creatinine or other concerns?
Are there any documented bleeding risks, falls history, or other contraindications relevant to apixaban use in this 84-year-old patient?
What follow-up actions were planned after the creatinine result — e.g., repeat test, nephrology referral, dose review?

candidate_highlights.risk_reason: Apixaban dose remains 5 mg BID despite meeting two of three criteria (age ≥80, weight ≤60 kg, creatinine ≥133 umol/L) requiring reduction to 2.5 mg BID per drug label.
candidate_highlights.suggested_action: Review and reduce apixaban to 2.5 mg twice daily unless contraindicated.

check_points.text: Check whether apixaban dose was reduced to 2.5 mg twice daily given that two of the following apply: age 80 or over, weight 60 kg or less, creatinine 133 umol/L or more.

reference.quote: Reduce the dose to 2.5 mg twice daily when two of the following apply: age 80 or over, weight 60 kg or less, creatinine 133 umol/L or more.

check_points.text: Confirm whether renal function was assessed prior to initiating apixaban, as recommended before starting therapy.

reference.quote:
Apixaban tablets (synthetic label for evaluation).

Reduce the dose to 2.5 mg twice daily when two of the following apply: age 80 or over, weight 60 kg or less, creatinine 133 umol/L or more.

Check renal function at least once a year.
